item.title: New CentOS 7 Maven Slave in docker-jenkins-slave
item.description: Docker & Jenkins Series: Using Docker Containers as Jenkins Nodes (2013-10-31) Docker Jenkins Slave Generator (2014-09-02) Caching Maven Local Repository in Docker (2015-03-13) New CentOS 7 Maven Slave in docker-jenkins-slave (2015-03-13) Docker-Jenkins-Slave 2.0 (DJS2) (2015-03-22) Today I pushed a new Jenkins slave template into docker-jenkins-slave named “centos7-java”. It’s based (thank you, Captain Obvious) on CentOS 7 and its purpose is to build Maven projects, so the image has Maven preinstalled.

item.title: Caching Maven Local Repository in Docker
item.description: Docker & Jenkins Series: Using Docker Containers as Jenkins Nodes (2013-10-31) Docker Jenkins Slave Generator (2014-09-02) Caching Maven Local Repository in Docker (2015-03-13) New CentOS 7 Maven Slave in docker-jenkins-slave (2015-03-13) Docker-Jenkins-Slave 2.0 (DJS2) (2015-03-22) I’m using Docker instances as Jenkins slaves and run my containers like: # docker run -d --name="Chewbakka" antigluk/jenkins-slave-centos7-java -labels docker-centos7-java -name "Chewbakka" (actually, I do it using docker-jenkins-slave) However, it doesn’t make sense to keep maven local repository in every container.
